view.lede: The Tight Track, left-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (sharp oval with a sprint spur), with the bigger of its two stand sides. A small, sharp oval of about 1m2f with tight turns, a 3f run-in and a 6f sprint course carried on from the home straight. Dressed as a market-town course.
notes: Catterick, Musselburgh, Southwell, Thirsk, Ripon, Windsor.
About 10.5f round, a 2.9f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Market-town course: old small stands and pavilions clustered round the winning post, near the end of the straight, the crowd up to the rail, the festival in the infield opposite.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
